data.ruling:
The refutation stands, and its scope is function. The datasheet verifier's refutation holds. The stock verifier returned incomplete with no refutation.

The requirement is in the R3 row (Research.md@e13f5f6:281). The external module must be qualified for "safe operating area during turn-off" at every current up to its highest. V48 sets that current at 600 A on the external path (owner, 2026-09-28).

The claimed pass rests on 600 A dividing equally over 5 parallel modules, 120 A each. That is set against the single-pulse 100 us line of Fig. 14. My own reading at 600 dpi puts that line at 136 A (135.9 to 136.5 A) at 85 V, with TC 25 degC, TJ 175 degC, single pulse. That agrees with the 134 A in the record and the verifier's 136 to 138 A. 100 us is the shortest line drawn.

The 120 A figure holds only if the current divides equally. The datasheet states no division:
- VGS(th) spans 2.2 V to 3.8 V at ID 750 uA.
- gfs is 94 S typical at ID 20 A.
- Fig. 5 (transfer characteristics, VDS 20 V) puts the TJ 175 degC curve left of the TJ 25 degC curve across the 0 to 400 A range drawn. At 120 A a hotter module therefore conducts at a lower VGS and takes more current. In the saturation region of a controlled 34 us turn-off, that is positive thermal feedback, not self-balancing.
- P2's own record says "Sharing at turn-off not stated".

The margin between 120 A and 136 A is 13 % at TC 25 degC. Any imbalance above that is outside the drawn SOA, and the datasheet bounds none. Case temperature above 25 degC shrinks the margin further. It would be above 25 degC after 300 A for 30 s (V50), which the record puts at 11 W a module. The verifier's 115 A at TC 50 degC depends on a 50 degC ambient that V38 leaves for research, so I do not rest the ruling on it. The sharing ground is enough without it.

A ramp-down pulse of 34 us is milder than a 100 us rectangle. But no sharing figure exists to carry that argument, and the datasheet does not make it. So the datasheet does not show that the module turns off 600 A inside its SOA.

The failure concerns this function's current and its parallel arrangement, not the part itself. The part-level checks pass:
- Digi-Key ProductStatus Active, discontinued false, end_of_life false.
- The Vishay page carries no status. The Lifecycle check records that as not read and reported to the owner, not as a failure.
- Vishay is on S1.
- It is off the board, with no LCSC number.

- Thermal table: RthJC 0.23 degC/W max, RthCS 0.1 typical.
- No statement on paralleling or current sharing anywhere in the 6 pages.
